title: The Hidden Bloat in Machine Learning Systems
problem: ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, MXNet) ship highly bloated shared libraries with large amounts of unused GPU and CPU code, wasting memory, increasing load times, and degrading performance.
motivation: Software bloat in ML systems has been overlooked compared to general software. GPU code bloat is a primary contributor that existing debloating tools ignore. The hardware-architecture mismatch (code compiled for many GPU architectures but only one used at runtime) is the root cause.
method: Negativa-ML hooks into CUDA's cuModuleGetFunction API—a checkpoint where GPU kernels load before execution—to detect which GPU functions actually run on each workload. It removes bloat at two levels: individual functions and entire cubin files (compiled GPU binaries). CPU code bloat is identified using standard call-graph analysis. The method was tested on 4 ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, MXNet), 10 real workloads, and 300+ shared libraries.
key_novelty: This is the first tool to locate and remove GPU code bloat from ML libraries by observing which kernels are actually used, revealing that GPU waste (not CPU waste) is the primary source of bloat due to hardware-architecture mismatch.
contributions: Negativa-ML: novel tool detecting and removing bloat from GPU and CPU code in ML shared libraries
cuModuleGetFunction hook technique for runtime GPU kernel usage detection
Cubin and element-level granularity for GPU code localization and removal
Identification of hardware-architecture mismatch as the primary cause of GPU bloat
Up to 75% reduction in GPU code size, up to 72% in CPU code size
Up to 55% total file size reduction
Performance improvements: up to 74.6% CPU memory reduction, 69.6% GPU memory reduction, 44.6% execution time reduction
baselines: Full unmodified ML framework shared libraries (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, MXNet)
limitations: Debloating is workload-specific; different workloads may require different debloated builds; hooking cuModuleGetFunction requires coverage of all target workloads during profiling; dynamic/JIT-compiled kernels may not be captured; requires rebuilding libraries.
